stories.title: Unit-string canonicalization -- volt not V (D-4, migration-first)
stories.completionNotes: US-455 unit-string canonicalization SHIPPED + 125 targeted tests GREEN + ruff clean on all 11 files (commit ff1cf20). CANONICAL DECISION (grounded, not fabricated): the decoder-path units now emit the python-obd NATIVE unit string, so a physical unit has ONE canonical label across BOTH write paths -- the legacy path already stores str(response.unit) = native (logger.py:490-502 _extractUnit), while the decoder path was overriding it with a hand-written abbreviation. groundingRef: the decoder test fixtures feed the NATIVE unit as the decoder INPUT (tests/pi/obdii/test_decoders_v2.py: 'volt' line 175, 'kilopascal' line 157, 'second' line 136) and the decoder discarded it for 'V'/'kPa'/'s' -- so 'volt'/'kilopascal'/'second' are python-obd's own rendering, directly grounded (python-obd is NOT installed in the dev env, so the fixtures are the SSOT for the native strings). MAPPING: 'V'->'volt' (decodeBatteryVoltage + decodeO2PostCatVoltage), 'kPa'->'kilopascal' (decodeBarometricKpa), 's'->'second' (decodeRuntimeSec). TWO REAL COLLISIONS in actually-polled data justify the set (both params in pollingTiers): voltage = legacy O2_B1S1 'volt' (tier3, native path) vs decoder 'V' (BATTERY_V tier3 + O2_B1S2 tier2); pressure = legacy INTAKE_PRESSURE 'kilopascal' (tier4, native) vs decoder 'kPa' (BAROMETRIC_KPA tier4). RUNTIME_SEC 's'->'second' has no twin but aligns to the SAME native rule so DISTINCT unit is uniformly canonical. NOT re-mapped (documented): DTC_COUNT 'count' -- python-obd STATUS carries no pint unit (fixture input is a bare status namespace, response.unit None), so 'count' has no native form + no colliding twin; and the enum textLabel OVERLOAD ('CL'/'OL'/'ON'/'OFF' written into the unit column for FUEL_SYSTEM_STATUS/MIL_ON via logger.py:307) is left INTACT per the AC 'keep the python-obd native enum overload (do not remove)'. SCOPE = source->data (the only durable scope, mirrors US-454): (1) SOURCE rename decoders.py so the Pi stops emitting abbreviations (4 return sites + DecodedReading docstring + header). NOTE: unlike US-454 this touched NO config.json -- units are decoder-emitted, not config-driven. (2) SERVER MIGRATION v0021 (forward-only DATA re-map): realtime_data.unit is the SOLE table carrying the Pi-emitted physical-unit string (confirmed vs models.py: RealtimeData.unit String(32) at :174 is the only bare `unit` column; drive_derived_signals speed_unit/distance_unit/accel_unit are server-computed 'km/h'/'km'/'m/s^2' labels on a different path -- untouched). Migration loops UNIT_REMAP {'V':'volt','kPa':'kilopascal','s':'second'} with an idempotent WHERE-guarded UPDATE per abbreviation + a zero-survivor SELECT COUNT post-probe per abbreviation (raises SchemaProbeError on a silent no-op so the runner never records success on a partial re-map). Registered #21 in ALL_MIGRATIONS. Hermetic FakeRunner test mirrors test_migration_0020 (coverage/ordering/idempotency/failure-modes) + de-brittled placement assert (present+sorted+after-v0020, not tail). (3) [ATLAS] 'unit is a typed LABEL never numeric': new tests/test_unit_is_typed_label.py = source-scan over ALL src/ .py asserting no float()/int()/Decimal()/numeric-compare of a `.unit` attribute (regex \.unit\b excludes pint's .units + the *_unit columns) -- confirmed ALREADY clean (zero violations pre-existing) -- plus a structural assert that RealtimeData.unit maps to a String type. SAFETY: grep confirmed NO consumer branches on the unit strings (no `unit == 'V'` / `'kPa'` anywhere in src/), so changing the emitted values breaks nothing downstream. Lockstep: 5 test assertions (test_decoders_v2 x4 + test_logger_v2_decoders x1) + 4 faithful BATTERY_V mock fixtures (idle-poll x2 + lifecycle/warm-restart e2e x2 -- fixture noise, unit not asserted, updated for a clean zero-remaining grep per the US-454 rename discipline). PM/DEPLOY GATES (bench-only, no MariaDB on Windows dev): 'deployed AND verified: SELECT DISTINCT unit returns canonical strings on chi-srv-01' = PM deploy-time gate (migration validated here via FakeRunner SQL-shape/idempotency/post-probe). BLAST-RADIUS FLAG for PM: this is a SHARED-DECODER change (Pi capture path, affects all captured rows) -> next Pi deploy stores native units; v0021 unifies history so old 'V'/'kPa'/'s' + new 'volt'/'kilopascal'/'second' rows converge. Run the full pytest suite at integration. mypy (strict) NOT run in-loop (not installed in dev env, sprint-wide) -> PM integration gate.
acceptance: canonicalize the unit STRING (e.g. volt not V); KEEP the python-obd native enum overload (do not remove); forward-only migration re-maps existing rows
[ATLAS] analytics treat unit as a typed LABEL, never numeric -- assert no code parses unit numerically
deployed AND verified: SELECT DISTINCT unit returns canonical strings; ruff clean in-loop; mypy (strict) at PM-integration

stories.title: static_data disposition + TD-061 (D-5, CIO-decided)
stories.completionNotes: US-456 static_data disposition RESOLVED -- DECISION: KEEP the table honest-empty (NOT drop); no TD-061 filed (that path is only for drop). 3 targeted tests GREEN + ruff clean on both touched .py files. GROUNDED RATIONALE (not fabricated): (1) static_data holds one-time OBD params keyed on the VIN (static_data.vin is NOT NULL FK -> vehicle_info(vin)); the VIN is read over OBD Mode 09; the current ECU MD326328 is Mode-09-SILENT (tuner knowledge: 'Mode 09 silent -- can't fingerprint via OBD') -> VIN un-gettable -> no valid FK -> no honest row can exist. (2) The empty table is ALREADY honest by design: StaticDataCollector.collectStaticData() (src/pi/obdii/vehicle/static_collector.py:220-230) queries the VIN FIRST and on a null response raises VinNotAvailableError + writes ZERO rows -- it never fabricates a placeholder VIN or a synthetic vehicle_info record (verified: _queryVin returns None when response.is_null(), :336-338; shouldCollectStaticData returns False on no-VIN, :147-149). An empty table here is an honest-instrument, faithful to the project's honest-availability/typed-NA discipline. (3) KEEP over DROP because: dropping cascades through an entire Pi subsystem (StaticDataCollector + vehicle/ package + ~15 exports + pi.staticData.* config keys + FK_static_data_vehicle + schema registration) -- grossly out of proportion to a size-S disposition with zero data-integrity benefit (table already empty); and the subsystem re-activates automatically the moment a Mode-09-capable ECU is connected (hardware-conditional, not dead). DELIVERABLES: (a) tests/pi/obdii/test_static_data_honest_empty.py -- 3 real-DB guards (temp SQLite + real INSERT path per I-040; only the OBD connection faked as Mode-09-silent since no real silent ECU on the dev bench): collectStaticData writes 0 static_data rows AND 0 vehicle_info rows on a null VIN + returns success=False/vin=None/errorMessage~VIN; shouldCollectStaticData declines; table still EXISTS post-disposition (keep, not drop). This makes 'honest-empty' a VERIFIED invariant, not just prose -- a future refactor that fabricates a placeholder VIN fails the guard. (b) database_schema.py: authoritative disposition doc-comment above SCHEMA_STATIC_DATA (the table SSOT). (c) docs/static-data-disposition.md: durable drop-vs-keep decision record with grounded rationale + re-evaluate triggers. NO config.json / no migration / no subsystem change (keep path). NOT a Refusal-Rule-1 blocker: the PM scoped a bounded 2-option choice with 'Decide + document', and the CIO already provided the decisive grounding fact (VIN un-gettable). mypy (strict) NOT run in-loop (not installed in dev env, sprint-wide) -> PM integration gate.
acceptance: [ATLAS: not F-104 -- CIO/hardware] VIN un-gettable (Mode-09-silent on MD326328): either DROP static_data (forward-only migration; file TD-061) OR keep honest-empty with a documented reason -- DECIDE + document the choice
if dropped: TD-061 filed + drop migration deployed AND verified (table gone); if kept: doc note why honest-empty
ruff clean in-loop; mypy (strict) at PM-integration
